websearch.engines.description: The SearXNG engines a search asks, by SearXNG's names. Behind Tor some refuse some exits (Google nearly always does); Test engines on this page shows which answer now. Yahoo serves Bing's results: asking both ranks Bing's first.

websearch.useTor.description: Send the engines' requests through Tor (the Tor plugin), so they see a Tor exit instead of this machine and a block is answered with a new circuit. Off: SearXNG asks the engines directly.

websearch.results.description: How many results web_search gives the AI when it does not say.

websearch.language.description: The language results are asked in (en, en-US, de, ...); auto lets SearXNG tell from the query.

websearch.timeoutSeconds.description: How long SearXNG waits for each engine (through Tor, answers take a few seconds).

websearch.newCircuitOnBlock.description: When engines refuse a search's Tor exit (a CAPTCHA, access denied, too many requests) and it comes back with almost nothing, or half the engines asked refused, search once more on new circuits (another exit).

websearch.stopAfterSeconds.description: SearXNG stops when nothing searched this long, and starts again with the next search (a few seconds). 0: it runs until IED stops.

websearch.instanceUrl.description: Use a SearXNG you run instead of starting one (http://host:port, or https:// with a certificate Windows trusts; json among its search formats). Tor is then that instance's business. Empty: IED runs its own.

websearch.python.description: The Python that runs SearXNG. Empty: IED's own (vendor/python).

websearch.searxngFolder.description: SearXNG's source folder (searx/ inside); its packages are the searxng-packages folder beside it. Empty: the one setup.bat installs (vendor/searxng).
